metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Lithuania

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for Lithuania using the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, stratified sampling of schools and students, and OECD estimates are produced to reflect the target population of 15-year-olds in participating countries/economies. The factsheet does not specify the exact student weight variable name or whether replicate weights were used, so the precise weight identifiers cannot be extracted from the provided text. Analysts using the OECD database should follow the PISA technical documentation (Reader’s Guide and annexes referenced in the note) for applying the appropriate sampling weights and uncertainty estimation; the factsheet itself focuses on reported international comparisons rather than re-estimation details.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a country factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 creative thinking results (means, proficiency levels, and relative performance) rather than presenting an original student-level predictive model with an explicitly described PV-based analysis pipeline. Plausible values handling is therefore not applicable for extraction here because the factsheet does not report how PVs were combined (e.g., Rubin’s rules) for a specific re-analysis. Missing-data handling is not reported in the provided text because the factsheet relies on OECD’s standard PISA estimation procedures documented elsewhere (Reader’s Guide and annexes).

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample for Lithuania is the set of 15-year-old students in Lithuania who completed the PISA 2022 creative thinking assessment (completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, and the creative thinking cognitive test was implemented in 64 countries/economies including Lithuania). The factsheet reports 7,257 students in 292 schools for Lithuania; no additional inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., item nonresponse thresholds or missing-data rules) are specified in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes creative thinking performance for Lithuania among 15-year-old students. PISA 2022 implemented a creative thinking cognitive test in 64 countries/economies (including Lithuania), with 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes: generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas, across four domain contexts (written, visual, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). For Lithuania, students scored a mean of 33 on a 60-point scale, on par with the OECD average. The factsheet reports proficiency distribution (80% at least Level 3; 26% at Level 5 or 6) and relative patterns across ideation processes and domain contexts, including higher relative success for generating creative ideas and for written/visual expression. It also highlights within-country gaps: socio-economic status predicts creative thinking (explaining 15% of variation), girls outperform boys by 3.5 points, and several beliefs/attitudes (e.g., fixed mindset vs perceived creativity malleability) relate to performance. The note flags that some countries/economies may have sampling-standard issues (asterisks), but Lithuania’s estimates are presented without such asterisk cautions in the provided excerpt.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is for an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet rather than an empirical ML study. The document reports descriptive and comparative statistics from the OECD PISA 2022 Database (means, correlations, variance explained, and proficiency shares) and does not provide an original predictive modeling pipeline, target variables, or ML algorithms to populate main_findings. Consequently, ML technique fields and confounder/predictor extraction are intentionally left empty, and PV/missing-data handling are not specified at the level required for an empirical re-analysis.
